section_desc: A company may be formed for any lawful purpose by seven or more persons, where the company to be formed is to be a public company; two or more persons, where the company to be formed is to be a private company; or one person, where the company to be formed is to be One Person Company (OPC). An OPC shall have only one member, one director and no public shareholding. The name of OPC must contain the words 'One Person Company'.

The memorandum of a company shall state: the name of the company with the last word 'Limited' for public company or 'Private Limited' for private company; State in which registered office will be situated; objects of the company; liability of members (limited by shares, limited by guarantee, or unlimited); amount of share capital and division thereof. The memorandum is the charter of the company — it defines its powers and objects.

A company incorporated after 2013 having share capital shall not commence business or exercise borrowing powers unless: a declaration is filed by a director that every subscriber to the memorandum has paid up the value of shares agreed to be taken by him; and the company has filed with the Registrar a verification of its registered office. Default: penalty of Rs 50,000 on company and each officer in default and Rs 1,000 per day during default.

section_title: Formation of companies with charitable objects etc.
section_desc: Where it is proved to the satisfaction of the Central Government that an association or proposed association is to be formed as a limited company for promoting commerce, art, science, sports, education, research, social welfare, religion, charity, protection of environment or any such other object, and intends to apply its profits or other income in promoting its objects, and to prohibit the payment of any dividend to its members, the Central Government may by licence issued, allow the association to be registered as a public company without the addition to its name of the word 'Limited' or the words 'Private Limited'. This is the Section 8 company under CA 2013 (previously Section 25 under CA 1956).

section_title: Prohibition on issue of shares at discount
section_desc: A company shall not issue shares at a discount except in the case of an issue of sweat equity shares. Any share issued by a company at a discounted price shall be void. Where a company contravenes this provision, the company shall be liable to a penalty of an amount equal to the amount raised through the issue of shares at a discount or five lakh rupees, whichever is less, and every officer in default shall be liable to a penalty of one lakh rupees.

section_title: Restrictions on purchase by company or giving loans for purchase of its shares
section_desc: A company shall not directly or indirectly purchase its own shares or specified securities unless the consequent reduction of share capital is effected under the provisions of this Act. Exception: buy-back of shares under Section 68 is permitted. A company shall not give any loan or extend credit or give any financial assistance for the purchase of or subscribing for any shares in the company or in its holding company if it would result in giving financial assistance for purchase of its own shares.

section_title: Power of company to purchase its own securities (Buy-back)
section_desc: A company may purchase its own shares or other specified securities (called buy-back) out of its free reserves; or the securities premium account; or the proceeds of the issue of any shares or other specified securities. Conditions: buy-back shall not exceed 25% of total paid-up capital and free reserves; the ratio of secured and unsecured debts after buy-back shall not be more than twice the paid-up capital and free reserves; all shares must be fully paid up; buy-back shall be completed within one year.

section_title: Prohibition on acceptance of deposits from public
section_desc: On and after the commencement of this Act, no company shall invite, accept or renew deposits under this Act from the public except in a manner provided under this Chapter. No company other than a banking company, non-banking financial company and any other eligible company as prescribed, shall invite, accept or renew deposits from public. Non-banking financial companies regulated by RBI have separate provisions. Eligibility criteria for accepting deposits include net worth requirements.

Every company shall keep and maintain registers of its members containing name, address, occupation, date of becoming member, date of cessation and other prescribed particulars. Where shares are held jointly, the joint holders shall be entered in the register in the order in which their names appear in the application for shares. Every company shall maintain a register of significant beneficial owners. Register must be open for inspection.

A general meeting of a company may be called by giving not less than twenty-one days' notice either in writing or through electronic mode in such manner as may be prescribed: Provided that a general meeting may be called after giving shorter notice if consent is given in writing or by electronic mode by not less than ninety-five percent of the members entitled to vote at such meeting. Notice shall specify the place, date, day and hour of the meeting and shall contain a statement of the business to be transacted thereat.

No dividend shall be declared or paid by a company for any financial year except out of profits of the company for that year or out of the profits of the company for any previous financial year or years arrived at after providing for depreciation or out of money provided by the Central Government or a State Government for the payment of dividend in pursuance of a guarantee given by that Government. A company which fails to comply with the provisions of section 73 and 74 shall not, so long as such failure continues, declare any dividend on its equity shares.

The financial statements shall give a true and fair view of the state of affairs of the company or companies, comply with the accounting standards notified under section 133 and shall be in the form or forms as may be provided for different classes of companies in Schedule III. At every annual general meeting, the Board of Directors shall lay before the meeting: a balance sheet as at the end of the financial year and a statement of profit and loss for that year; and a cash flow statement for the year.

The financial statements, including consolidated financial statement, if any, shall be approved by the Board of Directors before they are signed. The Board's report shall include: extract of annual return; number of Board meetings; Directors' Responsibility Statement; explanation on auditor's qualifications; related party transactions; conservation of energy, technology absorption, foreign exchange earnings; Corporate Social Responsibility policy and expenditure; statement on declaration given by independent directors.

Every company having net worth of rupees five hundred crore or more, or turnover of rupees one thousand crore or more, or a net profit of rupees five crore or more during the immediately preceding financial year shall constitute a Corporate Social Responsibility Committee of the Board. The CSR policy shall include list of CSR projects or programmes; manner of execution; monitoring mechanism. The company shall spend at least two percent of the average net profits of the three immediately preceding financial years on CSR activities.

section_title: Removal, resignation of auditor and giving of special notice
section_desc: The auditor appointed under section 139 may be removed from his office before the expiry of his term only by a special resolution of the company, after obtaining the prior approval of the Central Government in that behalf. The auditor who is proposed to be removed shall be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard. An auditor may resign by filing with the company and the Registrar a statement of reasons.

section_title: Company to have Board of Directors
section_desc: Every company shall have a Board of Directors consisting of individuals as directors. A public company shall have minimum 3 directors; a private company shall have minimum 2 directors; a One Person Company shall have minimum 1 director. Every listed public company shall have at least one-third of total directors as independent directors. The Central Government may prescribe the minimum number of women directors for prescribed classes of companies. Maximum 15 directors; can be increased by special resolution.

section_title: Right of persons other than retiring directors to stand for directorship
section_desc: A person who is not a retiring director shall, subject to the provisions of this Act, be eligible for appointment to the office of a director at any general meeting, if he, or some member intending to propose him as a director, has, not less than fourteen days before the meeting, left at the registered office of the company, a notice in writing under his hand signifying his candidature for the office of director or, as the case may be, the intention of such member to propose him as a candidate, along with the deposit of one lakh rupees.

Every director shall at the first meeting of the Board in which he participates as a director and thereafter at the first meeting of the Board in every financial year or whenever there is any change in the disclosures already made, then at the first Board meeting held after such change, disclose his concern or interest in any company or companies or bodies corporate, firms, or other association of individuals, which shall include the shareholding.
chapter_title: Meetings of Board and its Powers

section_title: Overall maximum managerial remuneration and managerial remuneration in case of absence or inadequacy of profits
section_desc: The total managerial remuneration payable by a public company, to its directors, including managing director and whole-time director, and its manager in respect of any financial year shall not exceed eleven percent of the net profits of that company for that financial year computed in the manner laid down in section 198. Where a public company has no profits or its profits are inadequate in any financial year, such company shall not pay to its directors any sum by way of remuneration except with the approval of Central Government.
chapter_title: Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel

section_title: Power of Registrar to remove name of company from register of companies
section_desc: The Registrar may strike off the name of a company from the register of companies where he has reasonable cause to believe that the company has failed to commence its business within one year of its incorporation; or the company is not carrying on any business or operation for a period of two immediately preceding financial years and has not made any application for obtaining the status of dormant company. Default strikes off: company is deemed to be dissolved.
chapter_title: Revival and Rehabilitation of Sick Companies

act: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
section_desc: In this Act: 'collective investment scheme' means any scheme or arrangement which satisfies the conditions referred to in section 11AA; 'depository' has the meaning assigned to it in the Depositories Act, 1996; 'listed public company' means a public company which has any of its securities listed on any recognised stock exchange; 'securities' has the meaning assigned to it in section 2(h) of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956; 'stock exchange' means a body of individuals whether incorporated or not, constituted for the purpose of assisting, regulating or controlling the business of buying, selling or dealing in securities.

act: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
section_desc: Subject to the provisions of this Act, it shall be the duty of the Board to protect the interests of investors in securities and to promote the development of, and to regulate the securities market, by such measures as it thinks fit. The measures include: regulating the business in stock exchanges; registering and regulating intermediaries — stockbrokers, sub-brokers, portfolio managers, investment advisers, depositories, etc.; promoting and regulating self-regulatory organisations; prohibiting insider trading and fraudulent and unfair trade practices; investor education and awareness.
chapter_title: Functions and Powers of the Board

act: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
section_title: Matters to be disclosed by the companies
section_desc: Without prejudice to the provisions of the Companies Act, SEBI may, for the protection of investors, specify by regulations the matters relating to issue of capital, transfer of securities and other matters incidental thereto; and the manner in which such matters shall be disclosed by the companies. All listed companies must make continuous disclosures to stock exchanges — quarterly financial results, material events, shareholding patterns.
chapter_title: Functions and Powers of the Board

act: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
section_title: Penalty for failure to furnish information, return, etc.
section_desc: If any person, who is required under this Act or any rules or regulations made thereunder fails to furnish any document, return or report to the Board; fails to file any return or furnish any information, books or other documents within the time specified therefor; or maintains or does not maintain books of account in the manner specified, he shall be liable to a penalty of one lakh rupees for each day during which such failure continues or one crore rupees, whichever is less.

act: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
section_desc: If any insider who: deals in securities of a body corporate on the basis of any unpublished price sensitive information; communicates any unpublished price sensitive information to any person, with or without his request, except as required in the ordinary course of business; or counsels, or procures for any other person to deal in securities of any body corporate on the basis of unpublished price sensitive information, shall be liable to a penalty of twenty-five crore rupees or three times the amount of profits made out of insider trading, whichever is higher.

act: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
section_desc: Without prejudice to any award of penalty by the adjudicating officer under this Act, if any person contravenes or attempts to contravene or abets the contravention of the provisions of this Act or of any rules or regulations made thereunder, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, or with fine, which may not be less than five lakh rupees but which may extend to twenty-five crore rupees, or with both.

In this Act: 'fire insurance business' means the business of effecting contracts of insurance against loss by or incidental to fire or other occurrence customarily included among the risks insured against in fire insurance policies; 'general insurance business' means fire, marine, and miscellaneous insurance business; 'life insurance business' means the business of effecting contracts of insurance upon human life; 'insurance company' means any company which carries on the business of insurance.

section_title: No person to begin or carry on insurance business without registration
section_desc: No person shall begin to carry on any class of insurance business in India and no insurer carrying on any class of insurance business in India shall continue to carry on any such business after the expiry of three months from the commencement of this Act unless he is registered with the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI). Violation: all contracts of insurance entered into by unregistered insurer are void.

act: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999
section_desc: Subject to the provisions of this Act and any other law for the time being in force, the Authority shall have the duty to regulate, promote and ensure orderly growth of the insurance business and re-insurance business. The functions of the Authority include: issuing certificates of registration to insurance companies; protecting interests of policyholders; specifying requisite qualifications and code of conduct for insurance agents; specifying standards for financial statements of insurers; imposing penalties for violation.

'Banking' means the accepting, for the purpose of lending or investment, of deposits of money from the public, repayable on demand or otherwise, and withdrawable by cheque, draft, order or otherwise. 'Banking company' means any company which transacts the business of banking in India. 'Commercial bank' means a banking company, State Bank of India, any subsidiary bank, or any corresponding new bank. 'Scheduled bank' means a bank included in the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act.

No company other than a banking company shall use as part of its name or in connection with its business any of the words 'bank', 'banker' or 'banking' and no company shall carry on the business of banking in India unless it uses as part of its name at least one of such words.

section_title: Board of Directors of banking company
section_desc: Not less than fifty-one per cent of the total number of members of the Board of Directors of a banking company shall consist of persons who have special knowledge or practical experience in respect of one or more of the following matters: accountancy; agriculture and rural economy; banking; co-operation; economics; finance; law; small scale industry; and any other matter the special knowledge of which would be useful to the banking company.

section_title: Power of Reserve Bank to give directions
section_desc: Where the Reserve Bank is satisfied that it is necessary in the public interest or in the interest of banking policy or to prevent the affairs of any banking company being conducted in a manner detrimental to the interests of the depositors or in a manner prejudicial to the interests of the banking company, it may, from time to time, by order in writing, give such directions to banking companies generally or to any banking company in particular, as it may deem fit.

section_title: Business which the Bank may transact
section_desc: The Bank may accept and hold deposits of money, including time deposits, from the Central Government, State Governments, banks, and other notified entities; purchase, sell, discount or rediscount bills of exchange and promissory notes; purchase, sell and deal in foreign exchange; grant advances or loans repayable on demand or on the expiry of fixed periods to the Central Government, State Governments, local authorities, and scheduled banks; buy, sell and deal in gold, gold bullion and silver.

Every bank note shall be legal tender at any place in India in payment or on account for the amount expressed therein. Every bank note issued by the Bank is a promise by the Bank to pay to the bearer the sum of rupees mentioned on the note. Bank notes are signed by the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India. The guarantee of legal tender is given by the Government of India.

Every scheduled bank shall maintain with the Bank an average daily balance of which the amount shall not be less than such percent of the total of the demand and time liabilities in India of such bank as the Bank may, from time to time, notify in the Official Gazette. This is the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR). The RBI uses CRR as a monetary policy instrument to control money supply in the economy. Interest is not paid on CRR balances.

Save as otherwise provided in this Act, rules or regulations made thereunder, or with the general or special permission of the Reserve Bank, no person shall: deal in or transfer any foreign exchange or foreign security to any person not being an authorised person; make any payment to or for the credit of any person resident outside India in any manner; receive otherwise than through an authorised person, any payment by order or on behalf of any person resident outside India in any manner.

Subject to the provisions of sub-section (2), any person may sell or draw foreign exchange to or from an authorised person for a capital account transaction. The Reserve Bank may, in consultation with the Central Government, specify any class or classes of capital account transactions which are permissible; the limit up to which foreign exchange shall be admissible for such transactions; and any conditions which may be placed on such transactions.

section_title: Enforcement of the orders of adjudicating authority
section_desc: Any person failing to pay the penalty imposed under this Act shall be liable to civil imprisonment. The penalty may be levied by sale of the assets of such person. Where the person is a company, the Directors of the company shall be liable to pay the penalty. Where any person establishes his inability to pay the penalty for any reason, no civil imprisonment shall be imposed.

In this Act: 'complete specification' means a specification as described in section 10; 'invention' means a new product or process involving an inventive step and capable of industrial application; 'inventive step' means a feature of an invention that involves technical advance as compared to the existing knowledge or having economic significance or both and that makes the invention not obvious to a person skilled in the art; 'patent' means a patent for any invention granted under this Act; 'patentee' means the person for the time being entered on the register as the grantee or proprietor of the patent.

The following are not inventions: a discovery of a scientific principle; the mere discovery of any new property or new use for a known substance or of the mere use of a known process, machine or apparatus unless such known process results in a new product or employs at least one new reactant; a substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in the aggregation of the properties of the components; a mere arrangement or re-arrangement or duplication of known devices; any process for the medicinal, surgical, curative, prophylactic, diagnostic, therapeutic or other treatment of human beings or animals; plants and animals in whole or any part thereof other than micro-organisms; computer programmes per se; mathematical methods.

section_title: Persons entitled to apply for patents
section_desc: Subject to the provisions contained in section 134, an application for a patent for an invention may be made by any of the following persons, that is to say: by any person claiming to be the true and first inventor of the invention; by any person being the assignee of the person claiming to be the true and first inventor in respect of the right to make such an application; or by the legal representative of any deceased person who immediately before his death was entitled to make such an application.

Subject to the provisions of this Act, the term of every patent granted, after the commencement of the Patents (Amendment) Act, 2002, shall be twenty years from the date of filing of the application for the patent. Patents filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) also get 20 years from the priority date. No patent shall be renewed for any period beyond the 20-year term. Annual fees must be paid after grant to keep the patent in force.

At any time after the expiration of three years from the date of the grant of a patent, any person interested may make an application to the Controller for grant of compulsory licence on patent on any of the following grounds: that the reasonable requirements of the public with respect to the patented invention have not been satisfied; or that the patented invention is not available to the public at a reasonably affordable price; or that the patented invention is not worked in the territory of India.

Subject to the provisions of this section and the other provisions of this Act, copyright shall subsist throughout India in the following classes of works: (a) original literary, dramatic, musical and artistic works; (b) cinematograph films; (c) sound recordings. Copyright in India subsists for the life of the author plus sixty years from the beginning of the calendar year next following the year in which the author dies.

For the purposes of this Act, 'copyright' means the exclusive right subject to the provisions of this Act, to do or authorise the doing of any of the following acts in respect of a work or any substantial part thereof: in the case of a literary, dramatic or musical work — to reproduce, issue copies to public, perform in public, communicate to public, make any cinematograph film or record; in the case of an artistic work — to reproduce in any material form; in the case of a cinematograph film — to make a copy, sell or give on hire; in the case of a sound recording — to make any other sound recording embodying it.

Copyright in a work shall be deemed to be infringed when any person, without a licence granted by the owner of the copyright or the Registrar of Copyrights under this Act, does anything the exclusive right to do which is by this Act conferred upon the owner of the copyright; or permits for profit any place to be used for the performance of the work in public where such performance constitutes an infringement of the copyright in the work, unless he was not aware and had no reasonable ground for believing that such performance would be an infringement of copyright.

section_title: Certain acts not to be infringement of copyright — Fair Use
section_desc: The following acts shall not constitute an infringement of copyright: fair dealing with any work for the purposes of private or personal use including research; fair dealing for the purpose of criticism or review; fair dealing for the purpose of reporting current events and current affairs including the reporting of a lecture delivered in public; reproduction of any work for the purpose of a judicial proceeding; reproduction by a teacher or a pupil in the course of instruction; reading or recitation in public of any reasonable extract from a published literary or dramatic work.

In this Act: 'mark' includes a device, brand, heading, label, ticket, name, signature, word, letter, numeral, shape of goods, packaging or combination of colours or any combination thereof; 'service' means service of any description which is made available to potential users and includes the provision of services in connection with business of any industrial or commercial matters such as banking, communication, education, financing, insurance, etc.; 'trade mark' means a mark capable of being represented graphically and which is capable of distinguishing the goods or services of one person from those of others.

section_title: Absolute grounds for refusal of registration
section_desc: A trade mark shall not be registered if it is devoid of any distinctive character; consists exclusively of marks or indications which may serve in trade to designate the kind, quality, quantity, intended purpose, values, geographical origin, or the time of production; consists exclusively of marks or indications which have become customary in current language or bona fide and established practices; is deceptive or contrary to morality or scandalous; is likely to hurt religious feelings; is prohibited under Emblems and Names Act.

A registered trade mark is infringed by a person who, not being a registered proprietor or a person using by way of permitted use, uses in the course of trade, a mark which is identical with, or deceptively similar to, the trade mark in relation to goods or services in respect of which the trade mark is registered and in such manner as to render the use of the mark likely to be taken as being used as a trade mark. Passing off is a common law remedy for unregistered marks.

section_title: Removal of trade mark from register and imposition of limitations
section_desc: A registered trade mark may be taken off the register in respect of the goods or services in respect of which it is registered on the ground that: up to the date three months before the date of the application, a continuous period of five years from the date on which the trade mark was entered in the register or longer had elapsed during which the trade mark was a registered trade mark and during which there was no bona fide use of the trade mark in relation to those goods or services.

In this Part: 'claim' means a right to payment, whether or not such right is reduced to judgment, fixed, disputed, undisputed, legal, equitable, secured, or unsecured; 'corporate insolvency resolution process' means the process defined in Chapter II of Part II; 'corporate person' means a company, LLP, or any other person incorporated with limited liability; 'creditor' means any person to whom a debt is owed; 'debt' means a liability or obligation in respect of a claim which is due from any person; 'financial debt' means a debt along with interest, if any, which is disbursed against the consideration for the time value of money.

section_title: Initiation of insolvency resolution process by corporate applicant
section_desc: Where a corporate debtor has committed a default, a corporate applicant thereof may file an application for initiating corporate insolvency resolution process with the Adjudicating Authority. The corporate applicant shall file the application along with a proposed insolvency professional to act as interim resolution professional and books of account of the corporate debtor for such period as the Board may specify.

section_title: Management of affairs of corporate debtor by interim resolution professional
section_desc: From the date of appointment of the interim resolution professional, the management of the affairs of the corporate debtor shall vest in the interim resolution professional. The powers of the Board of Directors or the partners of the corporate debtor, as the case may be, shall stand suspended and be exercised by the interim resolution professional. Officers, managers and personnel of corporate debtor shall report to IRP and extend full cooperation to him.

The interim resolution professional shall after collation of all claims received against the corporate debtor and determination of the financial position of the corporate debtor, constitute a committee of creditors (CoC). The committee shall comprise all financial creditors of the corporate debtor. The voting share of each financial creditor shall be in proportion to the financial debt owed to them. All decisions of the committee shall be taken by a vote of not less than sixty-six percent of voting share of the financial creditors.

A resolution applicant may submit a resolution plan prepared on the basis of the information memorandum. The resolution plan shall provide for the payment of insolvency resolution process costs, repayment of financial and operational debts, management of affairs, implementation and supervision of the plan. The resolution plan must also provide for adequate means for supervising implementation and measures for prevention of fraudulent acts.

If the Adjudicating Authority is satisfied that the resolution plan as approved by the committee of creditors meets the requirements of section 30(2), it shall by order approve the resolution plan. The resolution plan once approved shall be binding on the corporate debtor and its employees, members, creditors, including the Central Government, any State Government or any local authority to whom a debt is owed. A resolution plan approved binds all stakeholders — it extinguishes claims not dealt with in the plan.
